title: split, as Python documents it
description:
Reproduce Python's `str.split` in C++ from its documentation.

```
split("  a  b ")       -> [a] [b]          (no separator: runs of spaces)
split("a,,b", ",")     -> [a] [] [b]       (a separator: empty parts kept)
split("a b c", " ", 1) -> [a] [b c]        (maxsplit)
```
hints: The docs say that without a separator, leading and trailing whitespace is ignored and `"".split()` is `[]`, while `"".split(",")` is `['']` (lesson 4.01).
With `maxsplit`, the rest of the string after the last split stays as one part, spaces included.
requirements: Two behaviours, exactly as the Python docs describe: with no separator, and with one.
Test the examples from the Python documentation page.
